javax.microedition.theme
Interface Skin

All Superinterfaces:
Theme
public interface Skin
extends Theme

Represents a skin, a collection of customization data specific to an application. Using skins with an application allows changing the appearance of the application's user interface without modifying the application code.

The Skin interface inherits from Theme and adds the application attribute and operations related to application elements.

Method Detail

getApplication

java.lang.String getApplication()

Gets the application this skin is for. The value returned is a name/version/vendor triplet that identifies the name of the application. This information is also used by applications to request a SkinManager instance.

Returns:
the application name
See Also:
SkinManager

getApplicationElement

Element getApplicationElement(java.lang.String feature,
                              java.lang.String role)
                              throws ElementNotFoundException

Gets an application element with the specified feature and role.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
Returns:
the element instance
Throws:
ElementNotFoundException - if an element with the specified feature and role was not found
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if feature or role is the empty string
java.lang.NullPointerException - if feature or role is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the skin is DRM protected

getApplicationElements

java.util.Enumeration getApplicationElements()

Gets the application elements of this skin as an enumeration of Element instances. If there are no application elements in the skin, this method must return an empty enumeration, not null.

Returns:
an enumeration of the application elements
Throws:
java.lang.SecurityException - if the skin is DRM protected

getApplicationFeatureRoles

java.util.Enumeration getApplicationFeatureRoles(java.lang.String feature)
                                                 throws SkinException

Gets the roles defined for a feature in this skin for its application elements. The roles are obtainable from the enumeration as java.lang.String instances.

If the feature is not supported by the skin for the application (i.e. is not one of those returned by the getApplicationFeatures(String) method), this method throws SkinException. If the feature is supported but there are no roles defined for it, an empty enumeration is returned.

Parameters:
feature - the feature name
Returns:
an enumeration of the roles of the specified feature
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if feature is the empty string
java.lang.NullPointerException - if feature is null
SkinException - if feature is not supported

getApplicationFeatures

java.util.Enumeration getApplicationFeatures()

Gets the features supported by this skin for its application elements. The features are obtainable from the enumeration as java.lang.String instances. If there are no supported features, this method returns an empty enumeration. Each distinct feature must occur exactly once in the enumeration.

Returns:
an enumeration of the features in this skin for the application

updateApplicationElement

void updateApplicationElement(Element newElement)
                              throws ModifyNotSupportedException,
                                     ElementException,
                                     SkinException

Updates an application element in the skin by replacing it with another element that has different content. The feature and role of the element to update are queried from the newElement parameter. Updates are not effective before the commit method is called.

If the implementation does not support modify operations, this method must throw ModifyNotSupportedException immediately. If no element with the specified feature and role is found, an ElementNotFoundException must be thrown. It is recommended that the checks be made in this order.

This method works different than the updateElement methods inherited from Theme in that UnsupportedContentException is not thrown because applications themselves determine what is supported in the application elements. Also, there are no customization policy checks for the same reason.

Parameters:
newElement - the element to be updated, primed with the new content
Throws:
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
ElementException - a subclass depending on the situation
ElementNotFoundException - if no element with the specified feature and role is found
java.lang.NullPointerException - if newElement is null
SkinException - if there is an error related to accessing the skin data
java.lang.SecurityException - if the skin is DRM protected, or the application does not have the permission to modify appearances
See Also:
Theme.commit()
